Getting started with translation in OpenStack Weblate

Use OpenStack Weblate to find a string, translate it, and check the saved translation. This example follows a Korean translation in the doc component of the i18n project. Choose an untranslated string to follow along. The example string is already translated.

The numbered boxes in the screenshots show where to click and what to check. The screenshots use the English interface of Weblate 2026.10.1.

On this page

  • 1. Open the site and sign in

  • 2. Choose a translation project

  • 3. Select the language and documentation component

  • 4. Open an untranslated string

  • 5. Read the source and its context

  • 6. Enter a translation while preserving RST syntax

  • 7. Save the translation

  • 8. Verify the saved translation in History

  • 9. Continue to the next string

  • If your screen differs from this example

1. Open the site and sign in

Open OpenStack Weblate. During this walkthrough, opening the site from a signed-out session redirected directly to the OpenInfraID sign-in page at https://id.openinfra.dev/auth/login.

The sign-in page explains that OpenStackID is now called OpenInfraID and that existing accounts can still be used. This guide assumes that you already have an OpenInfraID account.

  1. Enter your account email address in Email Address.

  2. Click the > button to continue.

The next screen prompts for your password.

  1. Enter your password in Enter Your Password.

  2. Click Continue.

  3. After authentication, you return to the OpenStack Weblate Dashboard.

Note

If you are already signed in, these steps may be skipped. The password screenshot was taken before entering a password, so the field is empty.

2. Choose a translation project

Open Projects in the top navigation bar and select Browse all projects. The Dashboard contents depend on your account's watched projects and other preferences. The full project list provides a starting point for new contributors.

Scroll through the project list and click i18n. This guide uses the i18n project, which contains internationalization documentation, as its example. To work on another project, select that project instead.

If i18n already appears in your Projects menu, you can open it directly. The Add project or plus button is not needed to translate an existing project.

3. Select the language and documentation component

In the i18n project's language list, click Korean (South Korea) (ko_KR). You may need to scroll down to find it.

On the Korean translation page, open the Components tab and select doc under master. Here, i18n is the project, master is the category shown in the navigation hierarchy, and doc is the documentation component to translate. Other projects may have different categories and component names.

The glossary component contains terminology. For the example sentence in this guide, open doc.

4. Open an untranslated string

Check that the breadcrumb reads i18n / master / doc / Korean (South Korea) (ko_KR). On the Translation tab, find Strings status and click Untranslated strings to open strings with an empty translation.

Common entry points include the following:

String status filters

Entry

When to use it

Untranslated strings

Translate strings that do not yet have a translation.

Unfinished strings

Work on untranslated strings or strings that need editing.

All strings

Browse strings, including those already translated.

Strings with any failing checks

Inspect strings flagged by automatic checks.

See the Weblate translation guide for more about translation entry points and workflows. The account used in this walkthrough could save translations directly. If your account can only submit suggestions, follow the participation instructions for that project.

5. Read the source and its context

In the editor, read the English (United States) source text first. Enter your translation in the Korean (South Korea) (ko_KR) field below it. The String information panel on the right shows the format and source location. For this example, they are rst-text and ../../source/infra.rst:80.

If the meaning is unclear, use Nearby strings below the editor to read the surrounding text. Follow relevant terminology in Glossary, if available. If you use Automatic suggestions, review them against the source before saving. No related glossary entries were shown for this example.

The selected source text mentions Zanata and Chinese locale names. These are part of the source's subject matter; the translation service used in this guide is OpenStack Weblate. Do not replace a service name in the source with Weblate merely because you are using Weblate to translate it.

6. Enter a translation while preserving RST syntax

Translate the human-readable text while preserving code, locale names, and reStructuredText (RST) references. The following markup was preserved in this example:

``zh-cn``
``zh-tw``
``zh-hans``
``zh-hant``
:ref:`handling_horizon_projects`

For example, do not translate the :ref: role name or the reference identifier. Keep the whitespace required by RST around inline markup, including before Korean particles following inline code or references. Preserve URLs, placeholders, commands, and other technical elements when they appear in the source.

The following Korean translation was entered during this walkthrough. Line breaks below are for readability; the translation was entered as one paragraph in Weblate.

이 작업은 horizon 관련 프로젝트에서 Zanata의 중국어 로케일(``zh-cn`` 및 ``zh-tw``)
이름을 ``zh-hans`` 및 ``zh-hant`` 로 변경합니다. 다른 프로젝트와 문서(horizon 관련
프로젝트의 문서 포함)에서는 ``zh-cn`` 및 ``zh-tw`` 를 그대로 사용합니다.
자세한 내용은 :ref:`handling_horizon_projects` 를 참조하세요.

Before saving:

  • Check that conditions, exceptions, and negations retain the source meaning.

  • Preserve backticks, reference identifiers, URLs, and placeholders.

  • Match terminology and writing style to the surrounding Korean translations.

  • Use Needs editing for a translation that still requires work. It was left unchecked in this example after reviewing the translation.

7. Save the translation

After you enter a translation, Unsaved changes! appears below the field. This means your changes have not yet been saved. In this walkthrough, Save and stay was used to save the translation and inspect the result without leaving the current string.

Save and navigation controls

Control

Action

Save and stay

Save the current translation and remain on the same string.

Save and continue

Save the current translation and move to the next string.

Skip

Skip the current string and move to the next one. Use a save button when you want to save an entered translation.

If a check reports a problem, compare the source and translation again. For RST documentation, pay particular attention to backticks, roles, whitespace, and link syntax. No failing check was displayed for the string saved in this walkthrough.

8. Verify the saved translation in History

Open the string's History tab. In this walkthrough, the new entry showed Translation added, with Current translation and State: Translated next to the Korean text. This confirms that the translation was saved rather than merely entered in the editor.

Note

This confirms that the translation was saved in Weblate. It does not confirm that the change has reached the source repository or the published documentation site. Repository synchronization and publication were not verified in this walkthrough.

Use the Copy permalink link to return to a particular string later. The example string's permalink opens the string saved in this walkthrough.

9. Continue to the next string

After using Save and stay, click the Next arrow in the top toolbar to move on. This walkthrough verified that the next untranslated string opened. When translating consecutive strings, you can use Save and continue.

The editor explains that search results stay fixed while you translate. A counter such as 1 / 51 may therefore remain unchanged immediately after saving a translation. To update the list to match the current filter, click Refresh results, the circular arrow to the right of the query field.

For each remaining string, read the source and context, enter a translation, review it, and save it. Before finishing your session, make sure your final changes have been saved.

If your screen differs from this example

  • The Dashboard is empty: Open Projects, then Browse all projects, and select the project directly.

  • The example string is missing from the untranslated list: It was saved during this walkthrough. Choose another untranslated string. To inspect the saved example, use All strings or its permalink above.

  • Untranslated strings is unavailable: Check whether any untranslated strings remain. Use All strings to review existing translations.

  • There is no save button, or only suggestions are allowed: Check your account permissions and the project's participation instructions. The controls shown here reflect the account used for this walkthrough.

  • A saved string still appears in untranslated search results: Verify the save in History, then click Refresh results to update the result list.

For more information about string states and context tools, see the official Weblate translation documentation.
